provider_decision.credential_model: user-supplied Brave Search API subscription token stored server-side only; BPM ships no shared key
provider_decision.why_selected: The service documents raw pre-extracted content for local RAG, supports POST, token/URL/snippet bounds, language preference, strict relevance and inline Goggles, and avoids BPM fetching result URLs.

terms_and_rights_policy.permitted_basis: Brave documents LLM Context for RAG and licenses Search Results for use inside Customer Applications.
required_restrictions: Use results only as transient per-query grounding in BPM; never cache them, persist them, build an index/database, or add them to local documentation or embeddings.
Do not train, fine-tune, evaluate, benchmark or otherwise improve any model or service with provider results; deterministic tests use project-owned fixtures.
Do not redistribute or expose raw provider result sets or snippets; display only the validated BPM answer, provider label and approved source citations.
Delete provider response content when the request terminates and cease use immediately if the account or provider terms end.
The Brave account holder accepts current provider terms and remains responsible for required privacy notices and lawful query submission.
terms_and_rights_policy.drift_trigger: Any endpoint/schema, pricing, rate-limit, terms, privacy, retention, ownership or RAG-use change requires a new review before the provider remains enabled.

privacy_disclosure.recipient: Brave Software, Inc. in the United States
sent: subscription token in a request header
privacy_disclosure.retention_warning: Standard Brave Search API query logs may be retained for up to 90 days for billing, troubleshooting and abuse prevention; Zero Data Retention is an enterprise option only.
privacy_disclosure.consent_requirement: M9-02 must show the exact outgoing query, provider identity, United States recipient and retention warning before each provider call; no consent means local-only.

source_policy.conflict_rule: External evidence cannot create or override BPM product support. A conflict with current local BPM documentation is labelled and abstains until M9-04 defines a reviewed resolution.

response_and_network_policy.sanitization: Every URL, title and snippet is untrusted external data; enforce the local URL post-filter, active-content stripping, encoded-control rejection and external source labelling before evidence packing.
response_and_network_policy.retention: provider body and derived snippets exist in memory for one request only and are cleared at terminal completion/cancellation/error
response_and_network_policy.failure: missing credential, no consent, overlong query, DNS/TLS/provider/schema/rate/timeout/filter/sanitization failure returns local-only without a retry

data_flow: deterministic BPM scope gate allows the exact-locale question
M9-02 obtains explicit consent for the displayed outgoing query and provider disclosure
server builds one fixed bounded POST and reads the user token from server-side configuration
Brave returns bounded pre-extracted grounding content from its index
BPM independently post-filters exact HTTPS host/path and sanitizes all external fields
accepted snippets enter a separate lower-priority external EvidencePack for one request
the local model generates under existing no-tools/output/citation controls
BPM displays a validated answer with explicit external citations and clears provider content

reproducibility.rule: Provider ranking and indexed content are time-dependent. BPM pins its request/source policy and tests only deterministic captured fixtures; live smoke tests are explicit, isolated and non-release-gating unless separately approved.

alternatives.reason: Closed to new customers and scheduled for discontinuation on 2027-01-01.
Retired and decommissioned on 2025-08-11; the suggested Azure AI Agents replacement adds a hosted-agent boundary.

SearXNG is a metasearch proxy rather than a stable index/provider; queries are forwarded to configured engines and site syntax is not enforced uniformly, while public instances add an unowned trust boundary.
Hosted answer generation duplicates and weakens the selected local-model, output-validation and privacy boundaries.
